In [[abstract algebra]], the '''trigintaduonions''', also known as the {{nowrap|'''32-ions'''}}, {{nowrap|'''32-nions'''}}, {{nowrap|'''2<sup>5</sup>-nions'''}} form a {{nowrap|32-[[dimension (vector space)|dimension]]al}} [[commutative property|noncommutative]] and [[associative property|nonassociative]] [[algebra over a field|algebra]] over the [[real number]]s.<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Saini | first1=Kavita | last2=Raj | first2=Kuldip | title=On generalization for Tribonacci Trigintaduonions | journal=Indian Journal of Pure and Applied Mathematics | publisher=Springer Science and Business Media LLC | volume=52 | issue=2 | year=2021 | issn=0019-5588 | doi=10.1007/s13226-021-00067-y | pages=420–428}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | title=Trigintaduonion | website=University of Waterloo | url=https://ece.uwaterloo.ca/~dwharder/Java/doc/ca/uwaterloo/alumni/dwharder/Numbers/Trigintaduonion.html | access-date=2024-10-08}}</ref>

== Names ==
The word ''trigintaduonion'' is derived from Latin ''{{linktext|triginta|lang=la}}'' 'thirty' + ''{{linktext|duo|lang=la}}'' 'two' + the suffix -''nion'', which is used for [[hypercomplex number]] systems. Other names include {{nowrap|''32-ion''}}, {{nowrap|''32-nion''}}, {{nowrap|''2<sup>5</sup>-ion''}}, and {{nowrap|''2<sup>5</sup>-nion''}}. Trigintaduonions have also been referred to as ''pathions'' (<math>\mathbb P</math>),<ref name=DSP>{{cite journal |last1=Valkova-Jarvis |first1=Zlatka |last2=Nenova |first2=Maria |last3=Mihaylova |first3=Dimitriya |title=Hypercomplex Numbers—A Tool for Enhanced Efficiency and Intelligence in Digital Signal Processing |journal=Mathematics |volume=13 |issue=3 |date=2025-02-03 |issn=2227-7390 |doi=10.3390/math13030504 |doi-access=free |page=504}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Hoppe |first=Travis |title=Irrelevant Topics In Physics |website=thoppe.github.io |url=https://thoppe.github.io/Presentation_Irrelevant_Topics_In_Physics/irr6.html |access-date=2026-06-06}}</ref> which Robert P. C. de Marrais had named in reference to the 32 paths of wisdom from the [[Kabbalah|Kabbalistic]] ([[Jewish mysticism|Jewish mystical]]) text ''[[Sefer Yetzirah]]''. However, this term is not generally accepted as standard terminology.

== Definition ==
Every trigintaduonion is a [[linear combination]] of the unit trigintaduonions <math>e_0</math>, <math>e_1</math>, <math>e_2</math>, <math>e_3</math>, ..., <math>e_{31}</math>, which form a [[Basis (linear algebra)|basis]] of the [[vector space]] of trigintaduonions. Every trigintaduonion can be represented in the form

:<math>x = x_0 e_0 + x_1 e_1 + x_2 e_2 + \cdots + x_{30} e_{30} + x_{31} e_{31}</math>

with real coefficients {{mvar|x<sub>i</sub>}}.

The trigintaduonions can be obtained by applying the [[Cayley–Dickson construction]] to the [[sedenion]]s.<ref name="Ensembles">{{cite web|url=https://mathsci.kaist.ac.kr/~tambour/fichiers/publications/Ensembles_de_nombres.pdf|date=6 September 2011|title=Ensembles de nombres|publisher=Forum Futura-Science|access-date=11 October 2024|language=fr}}</ref> Applying the Cayley–Dickson construction to the trigintaduonions yields a 64-dimensional algebra called the ''64-ions'', ''64-nions'', ''sexagintaquatronions'', or ''sexagintaquattuornions''.

As a result, the trigintaduonions can also be defined as the following.<ref name="Ensembles" />

An algebra of dimension 4 over the [[octonion]]s <math>\mathbb{O}</math>:
:<math>\sum_{i=0}^{3} a_i \cdot e_i</math> where <math>a_i \in \mathbb{O}</math> and <math>e_i \notin \mathbb{O}</math>

An algebra of dimension 8 over [[quaternion]]s <math>\mathbb{H}</math>:
:<math>\sum_{i=0}^{7} a_i \cdot e_i</math> where <math>a_i \in \mathbb{H}</math> and <math>e_i \notin \mathbb{H}</math>

An algebra of dimension 16 over the [[complex number]]s <math>\mathbb{C}</math>:
:<math>\sum_{i=0}^{15} a_i \cdot e_i</math> where <math>a_i \in \mathbb{C}</math> and <math>e_i \notin \mathbb{C}</math>

An algebra of dimension 32 over the [[real number]]s <math>\mathbb{R}</math>:
:<math>\sum_{i=0}^{31} a_i \cdot e_i</math> where <math>a_i \in \mathbb{R}</math> and <math>e_i \notin \mathbb{R}</math>

<math>\mathbb{R}, \mathbb{C}, \mathbb{H}, \mathbb{O}, \mathbb{S}</math> are all [[subset]]s of <math>\mathbb{T}</math>. This relation can be expressed as:

<math display="block">\mathbb{R} \subset \mathbb{C} \subset \mathbb{H} \subset \mathbb{O} \subset \mathbb{S} \subset \mathbb{T} \subset \cdots</math>

== Multiplication ==
=== Properties ===
Like [[octonion]]s and [[sedenion]]s, [[multiplication]] of trigintaduonions is neither [[commutative]] nor [[associative]]. However, being products of a Cayley–Dickson construction, trigintaduonions have the property of [[power associativity]], which can be stated as that, for any element <math>x</math> of <math>\mathbb{T}</math>, the power <math>x^n</math> is well defined. They are also [[Flexible algebra|flexible]], and multiplication is distributive over addition.<ref>{{cite arXiv | eprint=0907.2047 | last1=Cawagas | first1=Raoul E. | last2=Carrascal | first2=Alexander S. | last3=Bautista | first3=Lincoln A. | last4=Maria | first4=John P. Sta. | last5=Urrutia | first5=Jackie D. | last6=Nobles | first6=Bernadeth | title=The Subalgebra Structure of the Cayley-Dickson Algebra of Dimension 32 (Trigintaduonion) | date=2009 | class=math.RA }}</ref> As with the sedenions, the trigintaduonions contain [[zero divisor]]s and are thus not a [[division algebra]]. Whereas the sedenions have 84 zero divisors,<ref>{{cite arXiv | last=Reggiani | first=Silvio | title=The Geometry of Sedenion Zero Divisors | date=2024 | class=math.DG | eprint=2411.18881 }}</ref> the trigintaduonions have 1,260 zero divisors derived from 147 distinct triples.<ref>{{Cite arXiv| last=Wilmot | first=G. P. | title=Structure of the Cayley-Dickson algebras | date=2025 | eprint=2505.11747 | page=2 | class=math.RA }}</ref> Furthermore, in contrast to the octonions, both algebras do not even have the property of being [[Alternative_algebra|alternative]].

=== Geometric representations ===
Whereas [[octonion]] unit multiplication patterns can be geometrically represented by [[PG(2,2)]] (also known as the [[Fano plane]]) and [[sedenion]] unit multiplication by [[PG(3,2)]], trigintaduonion unit multiplication can be geometrically represented by PG(4,2).

[[File:Cayley-Salmon configuration g012.png|thumb|right|An illustration of the structure of the (15<sub>4</sub> 20<sub>3</sub>) or Cayley–Salmon configuration]]

=== Multiplication tables ===
The [[multiplication]] of the unit trigintaduonions is illustrated in the two tables below. Combined, they form a single 32×32 table with 1024 cells.<ref name="Weng_Gauge">{{cite journal | last=Weng | first=Zi-Hua | title=Gauge fields and four interactions in the trigintaduonion spaces | journal=Mathematical Methods in the Applied Sciences | publisher=Wiley | date=2024-07-23 | volume=48 | pages=590–604 | issn=0170-4214 | doi=10.1002/mma.10345 | doi-access=free| arxiv=2407.18265 }}</ref><ref name="Ensembles" />

Below is the trigintaduonion multiplication table for <math>e_j, 0 \leq j \leq 15</math>. The top half of this table, for <math>e_i, 0 \leq i \leq 15</math>, corresponds to the [[multiplication table]] for the [[sedenion]]s. The top left quadrant of the table, for <math>e_i, 0 \leq i \leq 7</math> and <math>e_j, 0 \leq j \leq 7</math>, corresponds to the multiplication table for the [[octonion]]s.

== Applications ==
The trigintaduonions have applications in [[quantum mechanics|quantum physics]] and other branches of modern physics.<ref name="Weng_Gauge" /> More recently, the trigintaduonions and other hypercomplex numbers have also been used in research on [[neural network]]s<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Baluni | first1=Sapna | last2=Yadav | first2=Vijay K. | last3=Das | first3=Subir | title=Lagrange stability criteria for hypercomplex neural networks with time varying delays | journal=Communications in Nonlinear Science and Numerical Simulation | publisher=Elsevier BV | volume=131 | year=2024 | issn=1007-5704 | doi=10.1016/j.cnsns.2023.107765 | article-number=107765| bibcode=2024CNSNS.13107765B }}</ref> and [[digital signal processing]].<ref name=DSP />
